tickets.title: Event-driven programming: action → handler → code
tickets.brief: Explain why the VB form designer changed the unit of work from constructing windows to responding to events.
requirements: Three clearly labeled user actions: click, type, resize. Each connects to a distinct Sub-handler box, then to an observable UI response.
Use the supplied Command1_Click / MsgBox example only for the click path. Other event names must be verified or remain descriptive labels, not fabricated classic-VB identifiers.
Distinguish event order from a continuously executing game loop. This is a GUI concept illustration, not a claim that Program.vb contains forms.
beats: 0–2 s: show a gray form and the three action labels.
2–6 s: activate Click → Command1_Click → message box.
6–10 s: demonstrate Type and Resize one at a time using descriptive handler labels.
10–12 s: hold the whole action → handler → response system.
checks: Every action reaches one handler and one result; arrows have visible direction.
The code displayed for Command1_Click matches SCRIPT.md verbatim.
The final hold explains the relationship without relying on motion or narration.
